title: Annotations reflection cannot reach, and processors that can

questions.stem: An annotation declared @Retention(RUNTIME) @Target(LOCAL_VARIABLE) is placed on a local variable inside process(). What can reflection read of it at run time?

options.text: getDeclaredAnnotations() of process() returns it, since it sits in that method's body.
options.says: A method's annotations are those on the method declaration; a local variable's annotation is not among them.

options.text: getParameterAnnotations() of process() returns it, since locals share the parameters' table.
options.says: That call covers the method's parameters, which are not local variables declared in its body.

options.text: None of them returns it: javac does not write it to the class file.
options.says: A declaration annotation on a local variable is not written to the class file (JLS 9.6.4.2), so RUNTIME retention cannot bring it back.

questions.stem: An annotation processor looks for @Builder, which is declared with @Retention(SOURCE), in the classes being compiled. What does the processor find?

options.text: Every use of @Builder, since processors work on the code being compiled.
options.says: Processors work on the source being compiled, where annotations of every retention are present; SOURCE only means the compiler drops it afterwards.

options.text: No use of @Builder, since SOURCE annotations are dropped before processors run.
options.says: SOURCE annotations are discarded after compilation, not before processing; processors see them in the source being compiled.

options.text: No use of @Builder, since processors read annotations from class files.
options.says: Processors work on the source being compiled, not on class files, so retention does not hide @Builder from them.
